newsitem.title: USA: Gensym sees Q2 oper loss before charge.
newsitem.headline: Gensym sees Q2 oper loss before charge.

text.p: Gensym Corp said on Thursday that it expects to report an operating loss of $0.20 to $0.30 a share before a restructuring charge of $2.0 million pre-tax, or $0.20 a share, for the second quarter ending June 30, 1997.
Revenues for the period are expected to be between $7.5 million and $8.5 million, Gensym said.
In the second quarter of 1996, the company reported revenues of $9.5 million and earnings per share of $0.11.
Analysts that follow Gensym had a consensus earnings estimate of a profit of $0.05 a share for the quarter, according to First Call.
A first quarter shortfall in bookings hurt second quarter results, in addition to the charge for severance and facilities consolidation, Gensym said.
Gensym chief financial officer Rick Darer said about 15 to 20 percent of the company's 300 employees would be affected by job cuts. Some of the job cuts will come from attrition.
In the United States, the software company is considering consolidating some of its executive space and it is reviewing international operations on a country by country basis, Darer said.
The changes would take place in "a relatively short duration," Darer said. Darer declined to be specific about the time frame for the job cuts and consolidation.
The company expects to release final results for the second quarter on July 31, 1997.
